title: Data Science Intern
description: You will join the Ecosystem Security team supporting initiatives related to fraud and abuse detection. You will explore relevant data, build a model, and measure its impact on how we protect players. Explore large transaction, account, gameplay, and behavioral datasets to characterize how a specific form of abuse works. Build and evaluate statistical or machine learning models to detect abusive activity at scale. Partner with operations analysts to translate investigation heuristics into model features, and measure results against confirmed cases and false positive rates. Build dashboards or monitoring so the team can track your signal without an analyst in the loop. Document data sources, methodology, and findings so the work can be extended after your internship, and present your results to the team. Experience with Python for data analysis, pandas and scikit-learn preferred. Ability to write SQL against large datasets to pull and shape your own data. A grounding in statistics and machine learning fundamentals, including classification and evaluation metrics beyond accuracy. A desire to develop strong data science and software development skills. Genuine curiosity about adversarial problems, specifically how and why people find ways to game a system. Good interpersonal and communication skills, with demonstrated ability to communicate technical findings within a team. The ability to react and respond effectively to constructive feedback. A flexible approach to rapidly evolving problems, and comfort working with messy or sparsely labeled data. Nice to have: exposure to any of anomaly detection, graph or network analysis, text classification and NLP, or sequence and time-series modeling. Nice to have: interest in games, live services, or online trust and safety. This internship has a flexible start date in 2027. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the posting location for the duration of the internship.
